title: DECam’s Deep View of Abell 3667
caption: The merging galaxy cluster Abell 3667, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This deep image shows Abell 3667, a galaxy cluster in the direction of Pavo that is actively merging. It was assembled from more than 28 hours of observations with the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera (DECam).

Galaxy clusters grow over time by merging with other clusters and groups. When two clusters collide, their individual galaxies mostly slip past one another, because the gaps between galaxies are so vast. The hot gas that fills each cluster, however, crashes together and can be shocked and heated in the process.

Gathering so many hours of exposure lets faint galaxies and structures build up in the image that a short observation would miss. DECam, built by the Department of Energy, works on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, which stands at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile, a Program of NSF NOIRLab.
